This is a basic example of what an Engulf of an area looks like...basically a PA candle will take out a prior high/low and then close below or above like so in these 2 examples on the chart..

From there it can be telling us it wants to go to the other side with price or it could be just a fake out.. Hey DT. I think the most important thing to note is maybe where the PA takes place. For one thing PA that starts away from HTF levels would be highly suspect for a FO to me. I think the part to consider to bump up your P/L would be to look at where the LTF PA takes place in relation to S/D on the left. Look at my example below. The first chart is the 240. See the FL on the left? Anywhere in or by the blue box price may turn.

Here is the 15min of that level. I think it would be important to look at PA on LTF if it occurs in reaction to the level in the blue oval, or the yellow box.

I think 2014 is going to be a good year for you.

I had some comments on one of your trades. Hindsight trading has us all being superstars, but it helps to understand why something might have failed. Of course, take my comments as just comments, nothing more.

In the chart below, the real area to be engulfed was to the left - the FL. That wasnt engulfed until you were actually already long. Your long position

v=ov9kH54Z-

was probably due to price stalling in that minor pullback, but that whole area is minor in

dM

movement to the wider price action. The FO that occurs a few bars later that pushes price through the true FL, would have been nice PA to get in on. Theres nice PA at the top there to reverse at the FL extent, and drop-base-drop that results in taking out the lows of this whole move. The base could have been one place to get in if you didnt want to miss the move, but then it should have been clear the best place to find sellers was really below the untested pivot to the left. If unsure, I would have placed part of my position at the base (though I wouldnt have traded the base in this image), and then look for PA to get long thereafter. Price sinks down to the lows, picks up those lovely sell orders and shoots to the moon. The push up from the lows was a signal to get in if you werent already in.

You had True FL broken -> price collapse->drop base drop->lows taken out, meaning buyers needed them, and this is the catalyst to the real major upswing. Theres clearly an SR in this initial push up that was also a means to get in on a lower timeframe too. No drawdown.

i have spent weeks pondering over this engulf stuff and the fakeouts. can someone let me know if i have cracked this or even just made a dent init lol! so ref engulfs im kind of seeing 2 types. lets say price forms a base and moves up and makes a new high in theory it has engulfed the highs and therefor places great emphasis on taking the 1st test of that base as it is now most likely a demand level. then also looking at price action on approach to a zone so lets say the market is moving towards a supply zone but keeps making new highs on the way therefor engulfs the highs on the way up and dosnt engulf a swing low before coming into the zone then the zone is more likely to fail! can anyone let me know if that adds up lol? i can see how super important this concept is a fakeout then is when price basically pokes through for example a resistance level and closes back below the resistance but in doing so has poked into the supply above the resistance and that then causes a reversal and realistically could explain the concept of stop hunts a bit more logically

Dear Druwainwright,

1510

price ALWAYS make new highs when approaching SUPPLY, doesn't it?

Good telltale sign that a level will hold is COMPRESSION, I strongly recommend you to do your homework on it If the price does not approach SUPPY / DEMAND in a compressed way, then you should wait for confirmation in the form of the engulf of last demand on the way up or last supply on the way down. This will give you a hint that price really wanna turn. And for me, personally, this is not enough. I like to wait for the first FTR, then it is usually a good trade upon return.

For more info u can look at my journal p. 13.

Keep up the good work (and don't forget the homework)
